# List of Character Variants of Iosevka

Double-storey `a` supports tapered `curved-bar-rising` and `curved-bar-falling` options,
for example `double-storey-serifless-curved-bar-rising` and
`double-storey-serifless-curved-bar-falling`. Its top hook also supports
`hook-vertical-cut` and `hook-diagonal-cut` terminals.
When both upright and italic `a` use a single-storey design, the forced
double-storey forms follow the selected `e` hook.

The `e`, `lower-schwa`, and `capital-schwa` selectors include vertical- and
diagonal-cut hooks. The `g` selector offers both cuts on single-storey and
open or disjoint double-storey designs.
The `ampersand` selector offers both cuts on upper-open and Et top hooks,
including upper-open tops combined with Et bottom variants.

The `capital-c` and `c` variants include `vertical-cut` and `diagonal-cut`
terminals, including independent top and bottom combinations. The `question`
and `glottal-stop` variants combine those cuts with smooth or corner bodies
(for example, `smooth-vertical-cut` and `corner-diagonal-cut`). For
`lower-final-sigma`, each cut applies only to the top and can be combined with
the existing tails, such as `vertical-cut-curly-tail`. The `cyrl-capital-e`,
`cyrl-e`, `cyrl-capital-koppa`, and `cyrl-koppa` selectors also have
`vertical-cut` and `diagonal-cut` options.

Capital K and the independent Cyrillic capital and lowercase ka selectors offer
`rounded-top`, `rounded-bottom`, `rounded`, and `curly-inverse` bodies with
serif choices. Their `rounded-connected` body uses cursive Zhe-style arms and
has no serif placements. Latin `k` also offers `rounded-bottom` and
`curly-inverse` with serif choices.

Greek Tsan follows the Cyrillic I selectors. `cyrl-i` also offers noncursive
`standard-tailed` and `asymmetric-tailed` bodies.

`lower-lambda`, `cyrl-capital-u`, and `cyrl-u` offer independent counterparts
to the `y` designs, including cursive vertical- and diagonal-cut hooks.
Lambda's y-based designs are vertically mirrored; its existing options remain available.

Cut terminals are also available for applicable `f`, `j`, `capital-j`, `r`,
`t`, cursive `y`, `long-s`, and traditional `lower-eszet` designs. Existing
palatal, retroflex, and implosive forms retain their original hooks.
For `i`, `j`, and `l`, diagonal-cut top and bottom terminals can be selected
independently of one another and of the existing diagonal-tailed designs.
The `lower-esh` selector likewise supports independent top and bottom
diagonal-cut terminals; its `tailed` option retains the uncut curved tails.
For `f`, descending bottom hooks have independent `bottom-vertical-cut` and
`bottom-diagonal-cut` options. Cyrillic `cyrl-ef` has independent top and
bottom straight, flat-hooked, rounded-tailed, diagonal-tailed, vertical-cut,
and diagonal-cut terminals, for example `top-diagonal-cut-bottom-vertical-cut`.
Other supported selectors include `two`, `three`, `five`, `six`, `nine`,
`capital-g`, `capital-s`, `s`, `capital-ezh`, `lower-ezh`, Cyrillic ze,
`section`, `at`, `pilcrow`, and `sterling`.

Regenerate these regular-weight SVG previews and this list with
`npm run build -- amend-readme:character-variants`.
